scenes.title: Paper Promise
scenes.text: A dollar bill is just paper. It only has value because we all agree to believe in it together.

scenes.title: Gold Gone
scenes.text: In nineteen seventy one, the link between the dollar and gold was cut, and money became pure trust.

scenes.title: Inflation
scenes.text: Prices creep up a little each year, so the same cash buys less. That quiet drift is inflation.

scenes.title: Purchasing
scenes.text: A hundred dollars does not buy what it did twenty years ago. The number stays, the value shrinks.

scenes.title: Created
scenes.text: Most money in the economy is created when banks lend, not when governments print notes.

scenes.title: Digital
scenes.text: Bitcoin asked a bold question: what if money needed no bank at all, just code and agreement?

scenes.title: Compound
scenes.text: Time in the market beats timing the market. Small steady amounts can grow into something huge.

scenes.title: Your Turn
scenes.text: Money is a game of trust and time. What is the smartest money lesson you learned the hard way?
